question:
Select the letter cluster that is related to the fourth letter cluster in the same way as the first letter cluster is related to the second letter cluster and fifth letter cluster is related to sixth letter cluster.

YJ : SD :: ? : RI :: BR : VL
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. XO.

GIVEN

• YJ : SD :: ? : RI :: BR : VL

SOLUTION

• Each letter of the first cluster is shifted by −6 to get the second cluster.

• Check: Y(25)−6=S(19), J(10)−6=D(4); B(2)−6=V(22, wrap), R(18)−6=L(12). Rule confirmed.

• So ? − 6 = RI, i.e. ? = R+6, I+6 = X(18+6=24), O(9+6=15) = XO.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Since first→second is −6, do the reverse on the known pair: RI + 6 → XO.

NOTE

• Fix the shift from a clear pair (Y→S = −6), then apply the same shift to the unknown side using position numbers A=1 … Z=26.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

JU, ?, DK, AF, XA, UV, RQ, OL
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. GP.

GIVEN

• JU, ?, DK, AF, XA, UV, RQ, OL

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: J, ?, D, A, X, U, R, O → decreasing by 3 (J10, G7, D4, A1, X24, U21, R18, O15).

• 2nd letters: U, ?, K, F, A, V, Q, L → decreasing by 5 (U21, P16, K11, F6, A1, V22, Q17, L12).

• Missing term = G and P = GP.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Sit the gaps: 1st letter −3, 2nd letter −5. From J,U → −3,−5 → G,P.

NOTE

• In two-letter series, track each column separately; wrap A→Z when you go below 1.

question:
In the following question, set of letter clusters are given. The letter clusters of each set are related to the letter clusters of the same set by some Logic/Rule/Relation. From the given alternatives, select a group of letter clusters which follows the same Logic/Rule/Relation.

(VN, TL, GO)

(KQ, IO, RL)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. (SX, QV, JE).

GIVEN

• Sample sets: (VN, TL, GO) and (KQ, IO, RL).

SOLUTION

• Rule: within a set, the two letters of every cluster are separated by the same gap.

• (VN, TL, GO): each pair is 8 apart (V–N=8, T–L=8, G–O=8).

• (KQ, IO, RL): each pair is 6 apart (K–Q=6, I–O=6, R–L=6).

• Option (SX, QV, JE): S–X=5, Q–V=5, J–E=5 → uniform gap of 5, and like the samples it has two forward and one reverse pair.

• Options 1 and 2 have mixed gaps (19,13,19 / 13,19,13) → rejected.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Take the letter difference in every cluster; the correct group keeps ONE constant difference throughout.

NOTE

• Set-based problems: the deciding rule is whatever is common to BOTH sample sets — here a single constant intra-cluster gap.

question: What will be the sum of number of Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays in April 2029?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 13.

GIVEN

• Month = April 2029 (30 days).

SOLUTION

• 1 Jan 2029 is a Monday; from 1 Jan to 1 Apr = 31+28+31 = 90 days, 90 mod 7 = 6, so 1 April 2029 = Sunday.

• 30 days = 4 weeks + 2 days ⇒ the first two weekdays (Sunday, Monday) occur 5 times; all others 4 times.

• Sundays = 5, Wednesdays = 4, Fridays = 4.

• Sum = 5 + 4 + 4 = 13.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• In a 30-day month only the 1st two weekdays repeat 5 times; if the 1st is Sunday, only Sunday among the three asked days gets the extra day → 5+4+4 = 13.

NOTE

• Odd-day method: fix the month's starting day, then the two ‘extra’ weekdays (days 29–30) decide which days appear five times.

question: Which of the following pairs of years have identical calendars?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 1929 and 1935.

GIVEN

• Find the year-pair with the same calendar.

SOLUTION

• Two calendars match when the total odd days between them is a multiple of 7 and both are the same type (leap/ordinary).

• Odd days from 1929 to 1935 = years 1929–1934: 1+1+1+2(1932)+1+1 = 7 ≡ 0 (mod 7).

• 1929 and 1935 are both ordinary years, so their calendars are identical.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• For a non-leap year, its calendar repeats after +6 years when a leap year sits in between (odd days = 7). 1929 + 6 = 1935.

NOTE

• Odd days: ordinary year = 1, leap year = 2; sum the odd days of the in-between years and check divisibility by 7.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. the box with 4 marks on top and 3 marks at the bottom.

GIVEN

• 1st figure → 2nd figure: top row 3 → 2 diamonds, bottom row 2 → 1 filled diamond (each row loses one element).

SOLUTION

• The relation reduces the count in each row by 1.

• 3rd figure has 5 vertical lines on top and 4 lines at the bottom.

• Applying −1 to each row → 4 lines on top, 3 lines at the bottom = Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Just subtract one element from every row of the third figure: 5→4 (top), 4→3 (bottom).

NOTE

• In figure analogies, count the number of elements per region first; the same numeric operation applies to the new figure.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. the hexagon filled with ‘+++’ over ‘+++’ (six plus signs).

GIVEN

• 1st figure → 2nd figure: the empty outline (house) is filled with an inner symmetric pattern of small signs.

SOLUTION

• The rule fills the plain outer shape with a symmetric block of plus signs.

• 3rd figure is an empty hexagon → it must be filled with the matching symmetric block: three ‘+’ on top and three ‘+’ below, all identical plus signs.

• Option has this balanced 3+3 fill; Option (3+2) and Option (2+2) are unbalanced and Option contains a ‘×’, so they are rejected.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Pick the option whose inner marks are symmetric (equal rows) and all of the same type (+), matching the neat fill of the second figure.

NOTE

• For ‘fill-the-shape’ analogies, match both the count/symmetry and the type of the inner marks.

question:
Select the option that is related to the third letter-number cluster in the same way as the second letter-number cluster is related to the first letter-number cluster and sixth letter-number cluster is related to fifth letter-number cluster.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

KT205 : NX605 :: LB125 : ? :: TO208 : WS608
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. OF525.

GIVEN

• KT205 : NX605 :: LB125 : ? :: TO208 : WS608

SOLUTION

• Letters: 1st +3, 2nd +4. Number: +400.

• Check KT205→NX605: K+3=N, T+4=X, 205+400=605. ✓

• Check TO208→WS608: T+3=W, O+4=S, 208+400=608. ✓

• So LB125 → L+3=O, B+4=F, 125+400=525 = OF525.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Same recipe everywhere: letters +3/+4, number +400. Apply to LB125 → OF525.

NOTE

• Treat the number as a whole (add 400), not digit-wise, exactly as the instruction states.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth letter-number cluster in the same way as the first letter-number cluster is related to the second letter-number cluster and fifth letter-number cluster is related to sixth letter-number cluster.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

SS20 : WY30 :: ? : KO60 :: AN80 : ET120
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. GI40.

GIVEN

• SS20 : WY30 :: ? : KO60 :: AN80 : ET120

SOLUTION

• First→second relation: 1st letter +4, 2nd letter +6, number ×1.5.

• Check SS20→WY30: S+4=W, S+6=Y, 20×1.5=30. ✓  AN80→ET120: A+4=E, N+6=T, 80×1.5=120. ✓

• The answer (first) relates to KO60 (second): reverse it — K−4=G, O−6=I, 60÷1.5=40 = GI40.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Number pattern ×1.5 fixes it fast: 60÷1.5 = 40; letters K−4, O−6 → GI40.

NOTE

• When the unknown is the ‘first’ term, invert the operation (−4, −6, ÷1.5) on the given ‘second’ term.

question: In a certain code language, ‘MORE’ is coded as ‘53’ and ‘TEST’ is coded as ‘66’. How will ‘ROAD’ be coded in that code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 40.

GIVEN

• MORE = 53, TEST = 66.

SOLUTION

• Code = (sum of letter positions) + 2.

• MORE = 13+15+18+5 = 51; 51+2 = 53. ✓  TEST = 20+5+19+20 = 64; 64+2 = 66. ✓

• ROAD = 18+15+1+4 = 38; 38+2 = 40.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Add letter values, then +2. ROAD = 38 + 2 = 40.

NOTE

• Verify a constant offset using both given codes before applying it to the target word.

question: In a certain coded language 'BRANS' is coded as 'DUFKO' and 'FAINT' is coded as 'HDNKP'. How will 'BLITZ' be coded in the same code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. DONQV.

GIVEN

• BRANS → DUFKO, FAINT → HDNKP.

SOLUTION

• Letter-wise shift pattern = +2, +3, +5, −3, −4.

• Check BRANS: B+2=D, R+3=U, A+5=F, N−3=K, S−4=O = DUFKO. ✓

• Apply to BLITZ: B+2=D, L+3=O, I+5=N, T−3=Q, Z−4=V = DONQV.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Memorise the shift string +2 +3 +5 −3 −4 and slide each letter of BLITZ accordingly.

NOTE

• Position-shift codes: find the shift for each place from one word, then reuse the same shifts.

question:
A series is given with one term wrong. Select that wrong term from the given alternatives.

DF586, GA500, JV414, MQ328, QL241, SG156
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. QL241.

GIVEN

• DF586, GA500, JV414, MQ328, QL241, SG156

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: D, G, J, M, ?, S should go +3 each → D, G, J, M, P, S; but the term shows Q, not P.

• Numbers: 586, 500, 414, 328, ?, 156 decrease by 86 → 586, 500, 414, 328, 242, 156; but the term shows 241.

• So the 5th term should be PL242, not QL241 → the wrong term is QL241.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Numbers drop by 86 (…328, 242, 156). The odd 241 flags QL241 instantly.

NOTE

• Check letter gaps and the number gap separately; a single mismatch in either marks the wrong term.

question:

BMC91, CND182, DOE273, ?, FQG455

The correct answer is: Option i.e. EPF364.

GIVEN

question: At what time (approximately) (in PM) for the first time after 12:00 PM minute hand and hour hand of the clock will make an angle of 40 degrees?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 12:07.

GIVEN

• Start at 12:00 PM (both hands together); required angle = 40°.

SOLUTION

• Angle between hands t minutes after 12:00 = 5.5 × t degrees.

• 5.5 t = 40 → t = 40 ÷ 5.5 ≈ 7.3 minutes.

• So the first time is approximately 12:07.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Just after 12, angle = 5.5 × minutes. For 40° → 40/5.5 ≈ 7 min → 12:07.

NOTE

• Relative speed of the minute hand over the hour hand is 5.5° per minute.

question: A clock is 8 minutes slow at 6 AM and 16 minutes fast at 6 PM. At what time (in AM) will it show the correct time?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 10:00.

GIVEN

• At 6 AM: 8 min slow (−8). At 6 PM: 16 min fast (+16).

SOLUTION

• From 6 AM to 6 PM = 12 hours = 720 minutes; total gain = 8 + 16 = 24 minutes.

• Gain rate = 24 / 720 = 1 minute every 30 minutes.

• To become correct it must gain the 8-minute deficit: 8 × 30 = 240 minutes = 4 hours after 6 AM.

• 6 AM + 4 hours = 10:00 AM.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Correct-time moment = 6 AM + (8/24)×720 min = 6 AM + 240 min = 10 AM.

NOTE

• Uniform gain: time to cancel the initial error = (initial slow) ÷ (total gain) × total duration.

question: In the following figure series, select the figure which can be placed at the sign of question mark (?) from the given alternatives.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. the fully symmetric floral figure (petals on all four sides with a centre square).

GIVEN

• A four-figure series where a curved petal/loop is added at successive corners of the inner square each step.

SOLUTION

• Step by step the design gains one more curved petal, rotating around the central square.

• Continuing the growth, the fifth figure is the complete design with petals evenly placed on every side — the 4-fold symmetric flower.

• This matches Option (top and side petals identical, giving full symmetry); the other options have unequal petals on top/bottom or sides.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• The series builds toward complete symmetry — choose the most balanced, fully-formed figure.

NOTE

• In ‘growing’ figure series, track what is added each step and extend it one more time, checking overall symmetry.

question: In the following figure series, select the figure which can be placed at the sign of question mark (?) from the given alternatives.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. the box with 3 small squares on top and 1 diamond at the bottom.

GIVEN

• Series (top squares / bottom diamonds): (1 / 3), (1 / 3), (2 / 2), (2 / 2), ?

SOLUTION

• Top squares increase by 1 every two figures: 1, 1, 2, 2, → 3.

• Bottom diamonds decrease by 1 every two figures: 3, 3, 2, 2, → 1.

• So the missing figure has 3 squares on top and 1 diamond at the bottom = Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Squares go up, diamonds go down (in pairs of steps): next = 3 squares, 1 diamond.

NOTE

• Count each element type across the series; opposite trends (one rising, one falling) fix the next figure.

question: Sum of the ages of 4 children born at interval of 3 years is 34 years. What is sum of the ages of youngest and eldest child?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 17 years.

GIVEN

• 4 children, common gap 3 years, total age = 34.

SOLUTION

• Let ages be a, a+3, a+6, a+9. Sum = 4a + 18 = 34 → 4a = 16 → a = 4.

• Ages: 4, 7, 10, 13. Youngest + eldest = 4 + 13 = 17.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• In any equal-gap set, youngest + eldest = 2 × mean = 2 × (34/4) = 2 × 8.5 = 17.

NOTE

• For an arithmetic progression, first + last = 2 × average of all terms.

question: Father’s age 10 years ago from present was 4 times of the age of his son 7 years ago from present. Son’s age after 14 years from present is 36 years. What is present age of father?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 70 years.

GIVEN

• Father (10 yrs ago) = 4 × Son (7 yrs ago); Son after 14 yrs = 36.

SOLUTION

• Present son’s age = 36 − 14 = 22.

• Son 7 years ago = 22 − 7 = 15.

• Father 10 years ago = 4 × 15 = 60.

• Present father’s age = 60 + 10 = 70.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Work backwards: son now 22 → 7 yrs ago 15 → father then 60 → now 70.

NOTE

• Convert every phrase to the present timeline first, then apply the multiple.
